cards.text: We're deep in a long run of proverbs from Solomon, Israel's king: short, punchy sayings, one right after another (Proverbs 10:1). Proverbs 18 opens with a man who isolates himself. Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer, and even I was talking to the rubber bands back there with me.

cards.question: The man in Proverbs 18:1 cuts himself off from everybody. Whose desires is he chasing?
True or false: Proverbs 18:1 says the man who isolates himself goes along with sound judgment.

cards.text: Next comes the fool, who does not delight in understanding. I bet if you hand this man a new idea, he hands it right back with a receipt.

cards.question: The fool in Proverbs 18:2 doesn't delight in understanding. What does he delight in instead?

cards.text: You ask this guy what time it is, and twenty minutes later you know his opinion on every parking garage in town. Then a wicked man walks in, and he did NOT come alone.

cards.question: Proverbs 18:3 says that with a wicked man comes ___ as well.

cards.text: Contempt, right on his heels, and shame is accompanied by disgrace. Bad news brings a plus-one, and the plus-one brings a PLUS-ONE.
Then the proverb reaches for water. The words of a man's mouth are deep waters, and the second half of the line brings in a bubbling brook.

cards.question: In Proverbs 18:4, the words of a man's mouth are deep waters. What does the bubbling brook stand for?

answers.text: The wealth of a rich man

cards.question: Proverbs 18:5 says showing partiality to the wicked is not good. True or false: it says depriving the innocent of justice is not good either.

cards.text: Then it's right back to the fool, and this time the proverb looks at what his lips bring him.

cards.question: In Proverbs 18:6, a fool's lips bring him ___.

cards.text: Strife, and his mouth invites a beating on top of it.

cards.question: True or false: Proverbs 18:7 says a fool's mouth is his ruin and his lips are a snare to his own soul.

cards.text: Next up, gossip, and the proverb describes it with FOOD, so you know I'm paying attention. A gossip's words are like choice morsels.

cards.question: Proverbs 18:8 says a gossip's words are like choice morsels. Where do they go?

cards.text: Now the proverb looks at the man who's slothful in his work. That's the guy who hits snooze so many times his alarm clock just gives up on him.

cards.question: Proverbs 18:9 says the man who's slothful in his work is brother to him who ___.

cards.text: The snooze-button guy and the wrecking-ball guy, BROTHERS, at the same family reunion. Now look up, friend, because the name of the LORD is a strong tower.

cards.question: Proverbs 18:10 says the name of the LORD is a strong tower. What do the righteous do?

answers.text: Run to it and are safe

cards.text: Then, right next door, the proverb puts up ANOTHER fortress: a rich man's wealth is his fortified city.

cards.question: Proverbs 18:10 gives the righteous a strong tower. Proverbs 18:11 says a rich man's wealth is like a high wall. Where is that wall?

cards.text: Like a high wall in his IMAGINATION, basically a fortress made of cookie dough that looks great right up until it gets warm. Next, the proverb checks a man's heart right before his downfall.

cards.question: In Proverbs 18:12, what is a man's heart like right before his downfall?
Proverbs 18:12 says pride comes before a man's downfall, but ___ comes before honor.

cards.text: Next up, the man who answers a matter before he hears it. Oh, he's got the answer, friend, he just hasn't got the QUESTION yet.

cards.question: True or false: Proverbs 18:13 calls answering a matter before you hear it folly and disgrace.

cards.text: Then the proverb turns inward. A man's spirit can endure his sickness, like a baker sneezing through a whole batch and STILL humming.

cards.question: Proverbs 18:14 says a man's spirit can endure his sickness. True or false: it says a broken spirit is easy to survive.

cards.text: Then come the discerning and the wise, and the proverb watches what their hearts and ears do with knowledge.

cards.question: In Proverbs 18:15, how do the discerning and the wise treat knowledge?

answers.text: They wait for it to arrive

cards.text: Then the proverb gets to doors. A man's gift opens them for him, no knocking, no waiting in the lobby.

cards.question: True or false: Proverbs 18:16 says a man's gift brings him before great men.

cards.text: Last stretch, friend. The first one to state his case seems right, and he is looking VERY confident.

cards.question: In Proverbs 18:17, the first one to state his case seems right until what happens?

answers.text: The judge hands down his ruling
The whole crowd takes his side

cards.text: You hear one side of a fight and you're ready to go to WAR for them, then you hear the other side and now you need to sit down. Next up, casting the lot, and it ends quarrels.

cards.question: Proverbs 18:18 says casting the lot ends quarrels. What else does it do?

cards.text: Then the proverb puts an offended brother right next to a fortified city, side by side, like they're standing in a lineup.

cards.question: True or false: Proverbs 18:19 says an offended brother is easier to win than a fortified city.

cards.text: Armies have taken fortified cities, but you try winning back a brother after you ate the last cookie in the tin. And disputes, the proverb says, are like the bars of a castle.
Then the proverb comes back to the mouth one more time, and this time it talks about what a man's words grow, like a crop.

cards.question: True or false: Proverbs 18:20 says a man's belly is filled from the fruit of his mouth.

cards.text: Now the stakes go ALL the way up, friend. This one little tongue is holding two very big things.

cards.question: Proverbs 18:21 says life and ___ are in the power of the tongue.
Proverbs 18:20 talked about the fruit of a man's mouth. True or false: Proverbs 18:21 says those who love the tongue will eat its fruit.

cards.text: Then a word about marriage: the man who finds a wife finds a good thing. And friend, that's not even the whole prize.

cards.question: In Proverbs 18:22, what else does a man obtain when he finds a wife?

cards.text: Next, the proverb sets a poor man and a rich man side by side. The poor man pleads for mercy, like somebody begging the bill company to waive just ONE late fee.

cards.question: In Proverbs 18:23, the poor man pleads for mercy, but the rich man answers ___.

cards.text: And the chapter closes on friends: a man of many companions may come to ruin. Hang on before you start deleting contacts, because this proverb isn't done.

cards.question: Proverbs 18:24 says a man of many companions may come to ruin. What does it hold up against all those companions?

answers.text: One friend who stays closer than a brother
A big crowd of loyal neighbors
A house full of hired servants
